qt: to the Commission Massimiliano Smeriglio (S&D), Pina Picierno (S&D), Brando Benifei (S&D), Dino Giarrusso (NI) Subject:

By means of Ministerial Decree No 161 of 11 April 20231, the Italian Ministry of Culture adopted guidelines for determining the minimum fees for licences for the use of goods delivered to state cultural institutions and places, introducing a tariff for the reproduction of photographs (paper and digital, including partial photographs) of state cultural goods for editorial use or merchandising. The decree went further than the guidelines developed in 2022 by the Central Institute for the Digitalisation of Cultural Heritage, which had made free of charge the publication in any editorial publication of images of state cultural goods2. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission consider that decree compatible with Article 6 of Directive (EU) 2019/1024 on the re-use of public sector information, which provides that ‘the re-use of documents shall be free of charge’, except for the recovery of ‘marginal costs incurred’ (paragraph 1) at most, for cultural goods, 'with a reasonable return’ to recover investments made?

What is more, does it take the view that the mechanisms provided for in the decree, in particular, proportionality between the tariff and print run and thus expected sales, are compatible with Article 14 of Directive (EU) 2019/790, which provides that reproduction of a work in the public domain ‘is not subject to copyright or related rights’?
at: (English version) to the Commission Massimiliano Smeriglio (S&D), Pina Picierno (S&D), Brando Benifei (S&D), Dino Giarrusso (NI) (7 February 2024) Subject: Compatibility of Ministerial Decree No 161/23 with Directive (EU) 2019/790 and Directive (EU) 2019/1024 By means of Ministerial Decree No 161 of 11 April 2023 (1), the Italian Ministry of Culture adopted guidelines for determining the minimum fees for licences for the use of goods delivered to state cultural institutions and places, introducing a tariff for the reproduction of photographs (paper and digital, including partial photographs) of state cultural goods for editorial use or merchandising. The decree went further than the guidelines developed in 2022 by the Central Institute for the Digitalisation of Cultural Heritage, which had made free of charge the publication in any editorial publication of images of state cultural goods (2). In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission consider that decree compatible with Article 6 of Directive (EU) 2019/1024 on the re-use of public sector information, which provides that ‘the re-use of documents shall be free of charge’, except for the recovery of ‘marginal costs incurred’ (paragraph 1) at most, for cultural goods, ‘with a reasonable return’ to recover investments made?

What is more, does it take the view that the mechanisms provided for in the decree, in particular, proportionality between the tariff and print run and thus expected sales, are compatible with Article 14 of Directive (EU) 2019/790, which provides that reproduction of a work in the public domain ‘is not subject to copyright or related rights’?

(23 April 2024) The Open Data directive (3) does not apply to all cultural establishments, but only to libraries, museums and archives. The rules for charging for reuse of data made available by these establishments are set out in Article 6 (5) and explained in Recital 38 of the directive. The income from such charges can cover the cost of collection, production, reproduction, dissemination, data storage, preservation and rights clearance and, where applicable, the anonymisation of personal data, together with a reasonable return on investment. In addition, prices charged by the private sector for the re-use of identical or similar documents can be considered when calculating a reasonable return on investment. It follows that libraries, museums and archives may charge above marginal costs to generate revenues for their normal functioning. Article 14 of Directive (EU) 2019/790 (4) requires Member States to provide that, when the term of protection of a work of visual art has expired, any material resulting from an act of reproduction of that work is not subject to copyright or related rights, unless such material is original in the sense that it is the author's own intellectual creation. Whether photos in question qualify as original would be for the national courts to determine. Recital 53 clarifies that cultural heritage institutions should not be prevented from selling reproductions of works of visual arts in the public domain. Besides this, the directive does not regulate the tariffs for reproductions of works in the public domain. The Commission is now assessing the conformity of all national laws implementing the Open Data directive.
